Petition Under Section 18 Of The Land Acquisition Act 1894 Award:
(By The Court U/S 26 Of Land Acquisition Act- 1894 On Reference
Petition U/S 18 Of The Act):
1.
This is a reference made by the Land Acquisition Collector (hereinafter referred to as 'LAC') under section 18 of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894 (hereinafter referred to as 'LA Act').

The reference was initiated on a petition made by the petitioner who was aggrieved by the amount of Ved Prakash (10/99-2000) vs Union Of India (Sannoth) on 5 February, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/151367663/
1 compensation awarded by the LAC vide above-referred award.

entities.text: Ved Prakash (10/99-2000) vs Union Of India (Sannoth)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
2. As per the reference, a large tract of land measuring 194 bighas 01 biswas of village Sannoth,
Delhi, was acquired by the Government for public purpose Growth Centre under Mini Master Plan Scheme.
The notification under Section 4 of The LA Act dated 01-06-1998 was issued.
The Declaration under Section 6 was made as mentioned on the index page.
Thereafter, above- referred award was announced by the LAC.

The LAC determined SIDHARTH MATHUR MATHUR Date:
2026.02.05 15:05:35 +0530 the market price of the acquired land as Rs. 2,33,333/-
per Bigha for A category land and Rs. 2,08,333/- per Bigha for B category land.

3. The petitioner, being dissatisfied with the market value determined by the LAC,
filed the present petition u/s 18 of the LA Act, seeking reference to this court.
The LAC forwarded the same to this Court for adjudication.

4. The case of the petitioner is that the petitioner was/is the owner/bhumidhar of land bearing khasra numbers as mentioned in the Statement u/s 19 of the LA Act that was annexed with the present reference and admitted by the petitioner during the stage of admission/denial of documents, situated within the Revenue Estate of Village Sannoth, Delhi (the said land).

The said land was acquired vide notification dated 01-06-1998.
5.

The petitioner has challenged the said award inter alia on the ground of inadequacy of compensation and incorrect assessment of market value of land inter-alia due to non- consideration of relevant factors like potentiality and fertility of the suit land, the surrounding colonies and developed areas, the market value of the adjoining areas/villages, the sale deeds of other lands
SIDHARTH
MATHUR MATHUR Date: 2026.02.05 15:05:40 +0530 of the contemporary period, nearness to the National Highway and industrial areas, the amenities available in the suit land etc.
6. The petitioner has prayed compensation at enhanced rate besides interest thereon and solatium in addition to the compensation.
7. An application u/o 1 Rule 10 CPC was filed for impleading RDD in the present suit.
The said application was allowed vide order dt. 11.12.2024 and RDD was impleaded as R-2 in the present petition and DDA was deleted from array of parties.
Thereafter, the Respondent no.1/the Union of India (UOI)/Land Acquisition Collector and Respondent no. 2/RDD contested the reference petition by filing their respective Written Statements.

8. The petition has been contested mainly on the ground that the LAC awarded adequate compensation to the petitioner after taking into consideration all the relevant factors and therefore,
LAC has correctly assessed the market value of the land after taking into account the market rates Ved Prakash (10/99-2000) vs Union Of India (Sannoth) on 5 February, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/151367663/
2 prevailing at the time of notification under Section 4 of LA Act.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
9. In written statement R-2/RDD also supported the SIDHARTH MATHUR MATHUR Date:
2026.02.05 15:05:45 +0530 contention of R-1/UOI.
10.
During admission-denial of documents, the counsel for petitioner admitted the statement given u/s 19 of the Act.

The following issues were framed :-
i) Whether the petitioner is entitled to enhancement in compensation, if so, to what amount?

OPP.
ii) Relief.

11. In evidence, the counsel for the petitioner on behalf of petitioner has adopted the evidence in a case titled as "Bal Kishan Vs. UOI.".
12.
The respondent no.1/Union of India, in its evidence, tendered the award as Ex. R1.
However, RE had not led on behalf of the R-2/RDD.

Accordingly, its right to lead RE was closed vide order dt.
05.02.2026.
13.
I have heard the Ld. Counsels for the parties and have also carefully considered the record.
My issue-wise findings are given hereinafter.

FINDINGS ON ISSUE NO. 1 :-
SIDHARTH MATHUR MATHUR Date: 2026.02.05 15:05:50 +0530 14.
Petitioner has contended that valuation of land determined by LAC is not reasonable as LAC has not adopted the correct method of valuation.
However, he has not led any evidence to support his contention as to how the LAC was wrong in fixing market value of land.
Ld. Counsel for the petitioner has only relied upon the judgment titled as Bal Kishan Vs. UOI, LAC No. 695A/08 (07/2008), decided by Ld.

entities.text: Bal Kishan Vs. UOI, LAC No. 695A/08 (07/2008)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Predecessor Sh. Amit Kumar vide his judgment dated 25-08-2012 and conceded that award be passed in terms of the said judgment and the same enhancement which was granted in the said judgment be also granted to him.
15. In Bal Kishan's case (Supra), an elaborate and detailed discussion was made before determining the amount of compensation.

With respect to the land of the village Sannoth (involved herein),
acquired through the same notification (as made herein), the ld. Predecessor Judge determined the market value of the land as Rs. 11,41,466/- per acre for category A land.

16. Since no different evidence has been led by the petitioner in the present case, I have no reason to give a different treatment to the land of the petitioner and to give a determination, different from that determined in the Bal Kishan's case (Supra).

3

entities.text: Ved Prakash (10/99-2000) vs Union Of India (Sannoth)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: SIDHARTH MATHUR MATHUR Date: 2026.02.05  15:05:55 +0530
The fair market value of the acquired land is adjudicated as @ Rs. 11,41,466/- per acre for category A land.

17. As far as land of Category B is concerned, Hon'ble High Court of Delhi in a case titled as Jai Singh Vs. UOI, LA No.266/08, decided on 23.08.2011 (Delhi High Court) had adopted/used a formula for determination of fair market value of Category B land vis-a-vis land of Category 'A'.

entities.text: Jai Singh Vs. UOI, LA No.266/08
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In Jai Singh's case fair market value of Category B land was adjudicated to be 2.5% less than fair market value of Category A land.
It is a matter of record that the land of Village Sanoth was in consideration before Hon'ble High Court of Delhi while deciding Jai Singh's case (Supra).
Hence, I find no impediment in adopting/relying upon the formula adopted by Hon'ble High Court of Delhi in said case.
In fact this court is under an obligation/duty to follow the orders passed by Hon'ble High Court of Delhi as well as Hon'ble Supreme Court of India.

On applying the formula adopted/used by Hon'ble High Court of Delhi in Jai Singh's case (Supra) the fair market value of category B land of village Sanoth acquired by same Notification is calculated to be 2.5% lesser than the market value
SIDHARTH
MATHUR MATHUR

Date:
2026.02.05 15:06:02 +0530 of category A land.

Hence, the market value of category B land of Village Sanoth acquired by same Notification is adjudicated to be Rs.
11,12,929.35/- per acre.

18. Besides above, petitioner shall be entitled to other statutory benefits under the LA Act viz. 12%
additional amount [as per section 23 (1A)] and 30% solatium [u/s 23 (2)] and will be entitled to interest under Section 28 of L.A Act on the fair market value @ 9% per annum for the first year and @ 15% for subsequent year till the making of payment of enhanced compensation by LAC as per provision of Section 28 of the Act.
Issue no. 1 is decided accordingly.
19. Findings on Issue No.2 - RELIEF

The share(s) of the petitioner(s) would be determinable as per the statement u/s 19 of the L.A.
Act proved on record and the said statement shall constitute a part of this award.
21. Reference petition stands answered.
Parties to bear their own cost.
A copy of this award be sent to the LAC for necessary information, action and expeditious compliance for remittance of the amount.
File be consigned to record room.
